newsitem.title: UK: Granada chairman sold shares to repair house.
newsitem.headline: Granada chairman sold shares to repair house.

text.p: Gerry Robinson, chairman of British media and leisure group Granada Plc, sold a large block of shares in the company in order to realise funds to refurbish his house in Ireland, company advisers said.
Earlier on Monday Granada's share price fell sharply on a bout of profit-taking that dealers said coincided with news of Robinson's sale of 57,500 shares at 914 pence each.

"It is a sale to raise cash for a particular purpose, namely the restoration of his house in Ireland," a company spokesman said, adding that all Robinson's other participations in company shares and options remained intact.
Granada shares closed down 18 pence on the day at 894-1/2 pence, having ended at 912-1/2 pence on Friday when Robinson made the transaction.
He retains an interest of 300,872 shares in Granada.
